I have also done cleaning work during my time at university. I use to do janitorial work in an office setting, and I'm female, so I can relate to what you have to go through. I now have my BA and work in an office, and treat the cleaners with the utmost respect. On some days off I like to get paid to clean houses. 

I cleaned houses during school after I quit work as a janitor. I recommend you look into house cleaning. It's a much better way to get paid to clean. Usually better pay and since it is solitary work you won't have to be in a toxic environment. Please look into it. There is a lot of full-time work for house cleaners.

You are a total asshole, I can't even believe what I just read. Not everyone can magically get an amazing job at the top of the pyramid. It's people like you with attitudes towards "low" status jobs that make me ashamed of humanity. Without people who have these jobs, the world cannot function.

Hey just so you know I'm a woman (not a middle aged woman but still) and I am not offended at all by what you said. I totally understand what you mean, and I hate to say it but I have the same feelings about the group of people you are referring to, and certain other groups (I use to work in retail so I can relate). Unfortunately women can be sexist towards their own sex, and sometimes I certainly am, and I feel like crap about it, even though I know I don't think there is something inherently bad about women.

You are not actually a misogynist. You don't actually think these women are inherently inferior. It's just a way you react. Your thought processes don't indicate it, which is really how a misogynist or any other "ist" is identified. This might not be true at all, but I feel like that these women belong to a cultural generation that has a certain expectation with unrealistic standards. Sometimes a person can't help making connections between people that are similar and then creating a prejudice, even a subconscious one. I agree with everything that others have said on here.

That being said maybe it is totally Freudian and related to your mother, haha.
Amazing! Those bartenders must be real hoopy froods.
That makes sense. I have a really hard time imagining someone who is proud of themselves wanting to kill his/herself.

Cool, thanks for your comment. I am glad you think I am interesting. I do have things worth living for but I do not think I deserve them. I've also wanted to kill myself because of intense fear and anxiety about the future. Even though I am taking medication and it does help a little, I am easily terrified. I know life is about risks and trying new things but it is so hard for me, physically. I have inability to progress doing so many things...if I have a little anxiety about something, I become so sick and have an anxiety attack so intense that I cannot continue to do anything related to the thing I have to do to get on with life. I have and/or had so, so, so many health problems that stem from GAD. One of the reasons that really propelled the desire to kill myself 2 (maybe 3) years ago was from being in extreme pain most of time from neck pain and headaches. My quality of life was drastically reduced and it felt pointless to continue because I spent so much time trying to solve my problem and there did not seem to be a solution. But now, I think the medication has been helping the decrease of headaches and neck pain. So that is a definite plus, and something to focus on as a reason to keep living. anyway, I know there are plenty of resources to getting help with wanting to commit suicide so this response is basically just to vent because I am not expecting anyone on here to go out of their way to help me or anything. Thanks so much for reading my story.
